newsitem.title: EGYPT: Syria says Israel wants Palestinians moved to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Israel wants Palestinians moved to Iraq.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam said on Wednesday Israel's growing friendship with Turkey was part of an Israeli plan which included expelling the Palestinians to Iraq.

In an interview published in Egypt, Khaddam said the Turkish incursion into northern Iraq last month was one element of the Israeli plan, while Turkey itself had designs on the oilfields around Iraq's northern city Mosul.

"Our view in Syria is that there is a strategic plan, not just to break the links between Arab states but also to break the national unity of each Arab country. This is basically an Israeli plan," he told the Egyptian government paper al-Ahram.

"The invasion of Iraq (by Turkish forces) is a fruit of this. We notice the acceleration of Turkish-Israeli contacts, then the rapidity of the (Turkish-Israeli defence) agreement, then came the invasion," he said.
Turkey says its only aim in northern Iraq is to hit Turkish Kurd separatists who have used the area as a base for attacks in southeastern Turkey.
Khaddam said: "Israel's aims are to dismember Iraq to be able to find a place for the Palestinians and to expel them there. This is an old idea from the first Zionist Congress" of 1897.

Analysts say the Turkish-Israeli defence agreement is aimed mainly at Syria, which has given shelter over the years to anti-Turkish separatists of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) and has longstanding disputes with Turkey over terrritory and water.
